standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to $B$ considered as a module over the polynomial algebra $A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ mapping onto it, it supplies openness of the flat locus and local finite presentation there.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case, the problem being local on $X$ and $S$ (proof lines 4189-4190).
Translate the morphism into a finite type ring map $A \to B$ and choose a surjection $A[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to B$, viewing $B$ as a finite module over the polynomial algebra (proof lines 4190-4192).
Apply the algebra result for finite type flat algebras to obtain the open flat locus and its local finite presentation (proof lines 4193-4194).

Presentation as a finite module over a polynomial algebra (proof lines 4190-4192).

difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a morphism locally of finite type, the flat locus is an open subscheme on which the morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, under the hypothesis that the weakly associated points of the base are locally finite (statement lines 4179-4186). The proof reduces to the affine case and re-reads the finite type algebra map as a finite module over a polynomial algebra, after which the algebra form of the statement applies. The reduction and the change of variables are the substance, so the claim is H2.
